events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Orbital by Samantha Harvey
events.overview:
Join Albany Park for a discussion of our 2026 One Book, One Chicago selection Orbital by Samantha Harvey.

In gorgeous, lyrical prose, Samantha Harvey follows six astronauts as they orbit the earth in the international space station over the course of a 24-hour period. At 90 minutes each, the craft completes 16 orbits in a day, revealing breathtaking views of earth from 250 miles above.

During their stint on the space station, the astronauts muse about the lives they left behind, family members they've lost, and the events that have led them to this improbable, awe-inspiring place.

events.title: Adult Book Discussion: The Grapes of Wrath by John Steinbeck
events.overview:
Join us to discuss the classic novel, The Grapes of Wrath, by John Steinbeck.
First published in 1939, Steinbeck's Pulitzer Prize-winning epic of the Great Depression chronicles the Dust Bowl migration of the 1930s and tells the story of one Oklahoma farm family, the Joads--driven from their homestead and forced to travel west to the promised land of California. Out of their trials and their repeated collisions against the hard realities of an America divided into Haves and Have-Nots evolves a drama that is intensely human yet majestic in its scale and moral vision, elemental yet plainspoken, tragic but ultimately stirring in its human dignity. A portrait of the conflict between the powerful and the powerless, of one man's fierce reaction to injustice, and of one woman's stoical strength, the novel captures the horrors of the Great Depression and probes into the very nature of equality…

events.title: Barack Obama Presidential Center
events.overview: The Barack Obama Presidential Center is a museum, library, and education project in Chicago to commemorate the presidency of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. The center includes a museum, community and conference facilities and houses the nonprofit Obama Foundation. Also included within the Center is a branch of the Chicago Public Library, and a community athletic facility, within a broad expanse of landscaped public park, gardens, and playground. A dedication ceremony was held on June 18, 2026, before opening to the public the next day, on June 19, Juneteenth.

events.title: Brookfield Zoo
events.overview: Brookfield Zoo Chicago, known until 2024 as simply Brookfield Zoo, and also known as the Chicago Zoological Park, is a zoo located in Brookfield, Illinois. Brookfield Zoo is owned by the Forest Preserve District of Cook County and is managed by the Chicago Zoological Society. It is the largest zoo in the Chicago metropolitan area and houses approximately 511 species of animals in an area of 216 acres. Brookfield Zoo opened on July 1, 1934, and quickly gained international recognition for using moats and ditches instead of cages.

stops.title: Willis Tower
stops.text: The Willis Tower, formerly known and still commonly referred to as the Sears Tower, is a 110-story, 1,451-foot skyscraper in the Loop of Chicago, Illinois, United States. Designed by architect Bruce Graham and engineer Fazlur Rahman Khan of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, it opened in 1973 as the world's tallest building, a title that it held for nearly 25 years. It currently remains the tallest building in Chicago, the third-tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, as well as the 26th-tallest in the world. Each year, more than 1.7 million people visit the Skydeck, the highest observation deck in the United States, making it one of Chicago's most popular tourist destinations. Due to its height and location, the tower is visible from a great distance.
stops.textKo: 윌리스 타워는 1973년 미국 시카고 일리노이에 지어진 마천루로, 지상 108층이며 높이는 442m이다. 2013년 뉴욕 시에 프리덤 타워가 건설되기 전까지는 서반구에서 제일 높은 건물이었다. 이 빌딩의 구조는 기둥이 없는 75피트 너비로 된 9개의 튜브로 이루어진 묶음튜브구조로 이루어져 있다. 2개는 50층 높이, 2개는 66층 높이, 3개는 90층 높이, 나머지 2개는 108층 높이이다. 종종 110층이라고 알려지는데 이것은 엘리베이터 박스와 지붕을 합한 잘못된 층수이며, 정확한 층수는 108층이 맞다.

stops.title: Franklin Center (Chicago)
stops.text: The Franklin Center is a 60-story supertall skyscraper in the Loop, the downtown neighborhood of Chicago. Completed in 1989 as the AT&T Corporate Center to consolidate the central region headquarters of the American Telephone & Telegraph Company, it stands at a height of 1,007 ft and contains 1.7 million sq ft of floor space. It is located two blocks east of the Chicago River and northeast of the Willis Tower with a main address of 227 West Monroe Street and an alternate address of 100 South Franklin Street. The building is the tallest constructed in Chicago in the last quarter of the 20th century. It is the 6th tallest building in Chicago and the 23rd tallest in the United States.
stops.textKo: AT&T 코퍼레이트 센터 또는 프랭클린 센터는 미국 일리노이주 시카고 루프 지역에 있는 높이 307m, 지상 60층의 초고층 빌딩이다. 시카고에서 5번째로 높은 건물이며, 미국 전체에서는 11번째로 높은 건물이다. 1976년에서 2000년 사이에는 시카고에서 가장 높은 건물이였다. AT&T가 소유하고 있으며, 회사의 본사 기능 통합을 위해 건축되었다.

stops.title: Home Insurance Building
stops.text: The Home Insurance Building was an early skyscraper that stood in Chicago, Illinois, United States, from 1885 to its demolition in 1931. Originally ten stories and 138 ft tall, it was designed by William Le Baron Jenney in 1884 and completed the next year. Two floors were added in 1891, bringing its height to 180 feet. Often cited as the world's first skyscraper, it was the first tall building to be supported both inside and outside by a fireproof structural steel frame, including reinforced concrete.
stops.textKo: 홈 인슈어런스 빌딩은 미국 시카고에 존재했던 마천루다. 세계 최초의 마천루라고 불린다.

stops.title: Millennium Park
stops.text: Millennium Park is a public park in the Loop community area of Chicago, Illinois, United States, operated by the Chicago Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events. The park, opened in July 2004, is a prominent civic center near the city's Lake Michigan shoreline that covers a 24.5-acre section of northwestern Grant Park. Featuring a variety of public art, outdoor spaces and venues, the park is bounded by Michigan Avenue, Randolph Street, Columbus Drive and East Monroe Drive. In 2017, Millennium Park was the top tourist destination in Chicago and in the Midwest, and placed among the top ten in the United States with 25 million annual visitors. Planning of the park, situated in an area occupied by parkland, the Illinois Central rail yards, and parking lots, began in October 1997.
stops.textKo: 밀레니엄 파크는 미국 일리노이주 시카고 북쪽에 위치한 공원이다.

stops.title: Aon Center
stops.text: The Aon Center is a modern supertall skyscraper located in the Northeast corner of the Chicago Loop, Chicago, Illinois, United States. It was designed by a partnership between architecture firms Edward Durell Stone and Perkins and Will and was completed in 1973 as the Standard Oil Building. With 83 floors and a height of 1,136 feet, it is the fourth-tallest building in Chicago, surpassed in height by the Willis Tower, Trump International Hotel and Tower, and St. Regis Chicago. The building is managed by JLL, which is also headquartered in the building.
stops.textKo: Aon 센터는 미국 일리노이주 시카고의 초고층 빌딩이다. 에드워드 듀럴 스톤이 디자인을 하였으며, 1970년에 착공하여 1972년에 완성되었다. 건물의 총 높이는 346.3m로, 83층이다. 윌리스 타워 및 트럼프 인터내셔널 호텔 앤 타워에 이어 시카고에서 세 번째로 높은 초고층 빌딩이다. 예전에는 아모코 빌딩, 스탠더드 오일 빌딩이라고 불리었다.

stops.title: Aqua
stops.text: Aqua is an 82-story mixed-use skyscraper in Lakeshore East, downtown Chicago, Illinois. Designed by a team led by Jeanne Gang of Studio Gang Architects, with James Loewenberg of Loewenberg & Associates as the Architect of Record, it includes five levels of parking below ground. The building's eighty-story, 140,000 sq ft base is topped by a 82,550 sq ft terrace with gardens, gazebos, pools, hot tubs, a walking/running track and a fire pit. Each floor covers approximately 16,000 sq ft. Aqua was awarded the Emporis Skyscraper Award as 2009 skyscraper of the year, and was shortlisted in 2010 for the biennial International Highrise Award.
stops.imageCredit: Unknown authorUnknown author / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

stops.title: Chicago River
stops.text: The Chicago River is a system of rivers and canals with a combined length of 156 miles that runs through the city of Chicago, including its center. The river is one of the reasons for Chicago's geographic importance: the related Chicago Portage is a link between the Great Lakes and the Mississippi River Basin, and ultimately the Gulf of Mexico. In 1887, the Illinois General Assembly decided to reverse the flow of the Chicago River through civil engineering by taking water from Lake Michigan and discharging it into the Mississippi River watershed, partly in response to concerns created by an extreme weather event in 1885 that threatened the city's water supply. In 1889, the state created the Chicago Sanitary District to replace the Illinois and Michigan Canal with the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal, a much larger waterway, because the former had become inadequate to serve the city's…
stops.textKo: 시카고강은 미국 일리노이주 시카고를 흐르는 길이 251km의 강이다. 원래는 시카고 중심부를 지나 미시간호로 흐르는 길이 251Km의 강이었다. 하지만 1900년에 시카고강 하구에 운하를 건설하여 운하의 바닥이 호수 수면보다 낮아지면서 물의 흐름이 거꾸로 바뀌어 오늘날에는 미시간호에서 물이 흘러 시카고 중심부를 지나 강의 북쪽 지류, 남쪽 지류와 만난다. 매년 성 페트릭의 날에는 시카고강을 초록색으로 물들이고 기념한다. 시카고강에는 도개교, 회선교, 승개교, 전개교 등 다양한 형태를 가진 45개의 가동교가 있다.

stops.title: Great Chicago Fire
stops.text: The Great Chicago Fire burned in Chicago, Illinois, United States, during October 8–10, 1871. The fire killed approximately 300 people, destroyed 17,000 structures across roughly 3.3 square miles, and left more than 100,000 residents homeless. The fire began in a neighborhood southwest of the city center. A long period of hot, dry, windy conditions, and the wooden construction prevalent in the city, led to the conflagration spreading quickly. The fire leapt the south branch of the Chicago River and destroyed much of central Chicago and then crossed the main stem of the river, consuming the Near North Side.
stops.textKo: 시카고 대화재는 1871년 10월 8일 토요일부터 10월 10일 화요일까지 미국 일리노이주 시카고에서 일어난 대형 화재이다. 이 화재로 300명 가까이 사망하고, 시카고의 9 km2에 달하는 지역이 불에 타고 10만 명 이상이 집을 잃고 이재민이 되었다. 이 화재는 19세기 미국에서 일어난 화재 사건 중 가장 큰 규모였으며, 시카고 도심 지역이 완전히 파괴되었지만 화재 이후 재건을 통해 시카고는 미국에서 가장 큰 경제 중심지 중 하나로 성장하게 된다. 이 화재가 일어난 날과 동시에 위스콘신주의 페스티고에서도 대화재가 일어나 그린베이 북부를 태웠다.
stops.imageCredit: Currier and Ives / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

events.title: Chicago History Museum
events.overview: Chicago History Museum is the museum of the Chicago Historical Society. The CHS was founded in 1856 to study and interpret Chicago's history. The museum and library have been located in Lincoln Park since the 1930s at 1601 North Clark Street at the intersection of North Avenue in the Old Town Triangle neighborhood, where the museum has been expanded several times. Long known as the CHS, the society adopted the name, Chicago History Museum, in September 2006 for its public presence.

stops.title: Century of Progress
stops.text: A Century of Progress International Exposition, also known as the Chicago World's Fair, was a world's fair held in the city of Chicago, Illinois, United States, from 1933 to 1934. The fair, registered under the Bureau International des Expositions, celebrated the city's centennial. The theme of the fair was technological innovation, as reflected in its, sleek, modern, Art Deco design, and in its unofficial motto "Science Finds, Industry Applies, Man Conforms". The exhibits at the fair intended to demonstrate how science connected with people's daily lives and how the marriage of science, technology, and industry would lead to national recovery and prosperity. Its architectural symbol was the Sky Ride, a transporter bridge perpendicular to the shore on which one could ride from one side of the fair to the other.

stops.title: Museum of Contemporary Art, Chicago
stops.text: The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago is a contemporary art museum near Water Tower Place in the Near North Side community area of Chicago, Illinois, United States. The museum, which was established in 1967, is one of the world's largest contemporary art venues. The museum's collection is composed of thousands of objects of Post-World War II visual art. The museum is run gallery-style, with individually curated exhibitions throughout the year. Each exhibition may be composed of temporary loans, pieces from their permanent collection, or a combination of the two.

It is home to numerous Polish artifacts, artwork, and embroidered folk costumes in its growing collection. Founded in 1935, it is one of the oldest ethnic museums in the United States and a Core Member of the Chicago Cultural Alliance, a consortium of 25 ethnic museums and cultural centers in Chicago. events.title: Shedd Aquarium
events.overview: Shedd Aquarium is a public aquarium in Chicago, Illinois, United States. It is one of the oldest continually operating non-governmental aquariums in the U.S. Opened on May 30, 1930, the 5 million US gal aquarium holds about 32,000 animals. It is the fourth largest aquarium in the Western Hemisphere and the 11th-largest aquarium in the world. The Shedd Aquarium is a highly ranked world aquarium and at one time was the largest indoor facility in the world.

events.overview:
Illinois Wesleyan University professor Chris Sweet will lead a talk on the role of the bicycle in Illinois history based on his new book: A History of Bicycling in Illinois: 160 Years of Booms and Busts (University of Illinois Press).

This talk will focus primarily on the bicycle boom of the 1890s and will examine the intersections of bicycling with social issues, politics, religion, sport, technology, and economics. Attendees will have an opportunity to view antique bicycles (including a penny-farthing!) and bicycle artifacts from the author's collection.

Chris Sweet is the Scholarly Communications and Information Literacy Librarian at Illinois Wesleyan University. He has written extensively about American bicycle history and topics within the field of library science. His experiences as a former professional triathlete and competitive cyclist helped to shape his bicycle history…

The Gradient
Written by Steph Del Ross

Presented by Campfire Repertory Theatre
Directed by Campfire Rep Associate Artist, Gina Cioffi

What happens when accountability becomes a business? In Steph Del Rosso’s sharp, darkly funny satire, men accused of sexual misconduct enter a futuristic rehabilitation center designed to reform them. When idealistic new employee Tess joins the organization, she quickly discovers that redemption becomes complicated when good intentions collide with technology, corporate ambition, and profit. The Gradient challenges audiences to examine power, forgiveness, and who gets to decide when someone has truly changed.

events.overview:
Why AI is Our Ultimate Test and Greatest Invitation?

This is a free and open event - we’ll watch a video and learn together, then discuss our opinions. You’ll come away with a better understanding of AI and develop your own ideas about this transformational technology.

Is AI ‘inevitable’? During this event, we’ll watch a video of Tristan Harris, co-founder of Center for Humane Technology, who explores AI’s profound implications, and makes the case for responsible development and greater societal awareness to avoid mistakes we’ve made in the past.

After the screening, we’ll have a facilitated discussion so you can weigh in with your own thoughts, concerns, and hopes.

Whether you’re an expert or simply trying to understand what living in a world driven by AI looks like, this is an excellent opportunity to discuss an important technology and its effects on your community.…

events.title: Chicago's Electric Blues Heritage and History: Diddley Bow Workshop
events.overview:
Diddley BowArchives Tie: The Black Ensemble Theater Company Records Collection

Chicago has a rich heritage of internationally renowned electric blues guitar players, such as Muddy Waters, Elmore James, Buddy Guy and many more. This workshop elevates this Chicago history by exploring the rise of the electric blues and some of its musicians’ very first musical instrument, the diddley bow, a one-stringed instrument sometimes also referred to as a cigar box guitar. Inspired by the history of Chicago’s renowned blues guitarists extracted from CPL’s archives, participants will build their own cigar box guitar. Musician Coco Elysses will present the diddley bow’s history, demonstrate its sound, and then instruct on how to build the instrument. Supplies will be provided. Chester Commodore was one of the most influential and acclaimed African American cartoonists of the twentieth century. During the nearly 50 years his cartoons appeared in the Chicago Defender, Commodore used his art to advocate for racial justice, human rights, and equality of opportunity. From the 1954 appearance of his world-famous first editorial cartoon (on the Supreme Court’s Brown v. Board of Education, featuring a hammer breaking chains); his work reached an international audience. More than that, his widely seen cartoons helped to bridge the gulf between the two "parallel universes" representing the separate worlds of Blacks and Whites in the twentieth century. Through his realistic and non-stereotyped depiction of human subjects, Commodore helped to end the "eight-ball" caricature that white cartoonists had used to depict African Americans.

Written by Steph Del Ross

Presented by Campfire Repertory Theatre
Directed by Campfire Rep Associate Artist, Gina Cioffi

What happens when accountability becomes a business? In Steph Del Rosso’s sharp, darkly funny satire, men accused of sexual misconduct enter a futuristic rehabilitation center designed to reform them. When idealistic new employee Tess joins the organization, she quickly discovers that redemption becomes complicated when good intentions collide with technology, corporate ambition, and profit. The Gradient challenges audiences to examine power, forgiveness, and who gets to decide when someone has truly changed.

events.title: When Studs Terkel Interviewed Me: What I Learned from Being Interviewed by the Pulitzer Prize-Winning Master Conversationalist
events.place: Harold Washington Library Center (Chicago Public Library)
events.overview:
Before becoming an oral historian himself, Mark Larson had the unique experience of being interviewed twice by Studs Terkel, once for Race (under the pseudonym Peter Soderstrom) and later for Hope Dies Last. Larson also sat with Terkel in the WFMT studio as Terkel conducted a live interview for his radio program. Drawing on these encounters, Larson recalls what it felt like to be Terkel's interviewee and what it was like to watch one of America's great listeners at work. He reflects on what Terkel taught him about asking questions and truly listening for what's underneath the answers, and how those experiences inspired his own work in oral history.

events.title: Meet Calvin B. Jones: Make a Mini-Mural
events.overview:
From 1976 to 1987 artist Calvin B. Jones along with fellow artist Mitchell Canton painted six murals on the South and West sides of Chicago. Jones was active in the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s and 1970s and aesthetically influenced by Chicago's AfriCOBRA collective (African Commune of Bad Relevant Artists), known for painting with bold dues they called Cool-Ade colors.
Learn more in our archives!

This fun, hands-on program welcomes families to discover the life and work of Jones while exploring the question “Whose murals get saved?” Together, participants will enjoy a guided mini‑mural activity inspired by Jones’s vibrant style, featuring bold colors and African print designs. It’s an engaging, creative experience for all ages, perfect for families who love to learn, make art, and explore Chicago’s cultural stories.

events.title: Meet Calvin B. Jones: Make a Mini-Mural
events.overview:
From 1976 to 1987 artist Calvin B. Jones along with fellow artist Mitchell Canton painted six murals on the South and West sides of Chicago. Jones was active in the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s and 1970s and aesthetically influenced by Chicago's AfriCOBRA collective (African Commune of Bad Relevant Artists), known for painting with bold dues they called Cool-Ade colors.
Learn more in our archives!

This fun, hands-on program welcomes families to discover the life and work of Jones while exploring the question “Whose murals get saved?” Together, participants will enjoy a guided mini‑mural activity inspired by Jones’s vibrant style, featuring bold colors and African print designs. It’s an engaging, creative experience for all ages, perfect for families who love to learn, make art, and explore Chicago’s cultural stories.

events.title: Sculpt Like Hunt and Perkins: A Creative Sculpting Workshop
events.overview:
This workshop highlights the accomplishments of Black Chicago sculptors with a spotlight on Richard Hunt and Marion Perkins. Hunt, a world-renowned sculptor and printmaker born in Chicago’s Woodlawn community and raised in Englewood, became one of the leading 20th century American artists. During his acclaimed 60-year career, he was a significant creator of public art in Chicago and across the U.S., with 160 public sculpture commissions in 24 states that included monuments of several notable figures.

Create your own mixed-media sculptures using clay, wire, cardboard, aluminum foil, and paint, inspired by Hunt’s abstract forms and his ability to transform metal into movement. Art activities may include:

events.title: What We Carry: A Collective Collage Workshop
events.overview:
Join us for this collaborative collage workshop exploring storytelling and connection through images. Teen will begin by choosing a personal theme, then use magazines to create visual responses while listening to music. Throughout the workshop, participants rotate between collages, adding their own interpretation to each theme. At the end, each collage returns to the person who started it, transformed by the collective. The experience encourages participants to release control, share perspectives, and discover how individual memories and ideas can become part of a larger collective story.

No prior art or collage experience is needed. Teens are encouraged to come with an open mind and a willingness to create, share, and respond to the ideas of others. All materials will be provided. This is a collaborative experience, so each teen's collage will be handled and contributed to by others…

events.overview:
What stories, sounds, and memories live in Ellis Park?

As our Anchor Curatorial Resident, Brother El is opening the studio each month to listen, connect, and record oral stories from Ellis Park and neighborhood participants. His practice begins with listening—to the rhythms already moving through a place and the people who give it meaning.

These open studio hours are an invitation to share a story, a memory, a perspective, or simply a conversation. Together, we’re building a living archive of the neighborhood—one that honors where we’ve been, reflects where we are, and helps imagine what comes next.

Community is not just the audience. Community is part of the composition.
Come listen. Come share. Be part of the frequency.

Written by Steph Del Ross

Directed by Campfire Rep Associate Artist, Gina Cioffi

What happens when accountability becomes a business? In Steph Del Rosso’s sharp, darkly funny satire, men accused of sexual misconduct enter a futuristic rehabilitation center designed to reform them. When idealistic new employee Tess joins the organization, she quickly discovers that redemption becomes complicated when good intentions collide with technology, corporate ambition, and profit. events.overview: Join the Chicago Park District and Bird Collisions in the Anthropocene for a bird-making workshop at Big Marsh Park. Participants will use upcycled cloth and donated materials to handcraft life-sized bird sculptures. Each artwork commemorates a real bird that lost its life after hitting glass — and connects each crafter with a bird species at risk of building collisions. ​​All of the artworks will be sewn together into a huge 300-foot-long “carpet” of birds that will travel the country as an educational art installation, raising awareness about the toll of building collisions on our bird populations. events.overview: Dr. Seuss Day is a celebration of "reading". Come listen to a story by Dr. Seuss and visit our activity stations for games and craft projects. This event is appropriate for children under 5 years old.
events.source: Chicago Park District (Chicago Data Portal)

events.title: Family Bingo Night at Cragin
events.posterCredit: Belmont Cragin, Chicago — Zol87 from Chicago, Illinois, USA / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview:
Get ready for a fun-filled evening of unlimited games of bingo and exciting prizes. Come dressed in GREEN and have a chance to enter the raffle for a ST. Patrick's Day Basket of Green Goodies. Fun for the entire family.

Children ages 6-14, must be accompanied by an adult. $5 fee is per child registered/parents are free. Registration includes unlimited games of BINGO, opportunities for prizes and refreshments.
events.source: Chicago Park District (Chicago Data Portal)
